- CENTRAL CONTRIBUTION:
This work introduces CancerST, a Tamagotchi-style serious game designed to enhance thyroid cancer awareness and management through gamified learning. It innovates by personifying the thyroid gland into an interactive virtual pet, offering a novel channel for disseminating information about thyroid health and promoting a ludic understanding of management strategies. The game was playtested with three thyroid health specialists, generating qualitative feedback affirming its potential as a useful educational tool.

- PROBLEM AND CONTEXT:
Thyroid cancer is one of the most common cancers globally, with projected 2024 estimates for the United States including approximately 44,020 new cases (12,500 among men and 31,520 among women) and around 2,170 fatalities (990 men and 1,180 women). It is often diagnosed at an average age of 51, with an incidence three times higher in women. Despite effective treatments for differentiated thyroid cancer, there is a noted research gap in academic literature concerning serious games for thyroid cancer awareness and management. This gap highlights an opportunity to leverage the engaging mechanics of virtual pet games like Tamagotchi, Om Nom: Merge, Pou, Pixel Petz, and My Talking Tom 2 for healthcare education.

- METHOD/SYSTEM:
CancerST is developed using the Unity engine for robust game development and animations, with original art created in Adobe Photoshop, and sound customized from a lullaby audio [25]. The game employs iterative development and responsive design, adhering to player-centric game mechanics and drawing inspiration from prior cancer and mental health-themed games. The main character is a virtual thyroid gland, automatically customized with randomly assigned health problems (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, thyroid cancer (phases 1-4), thyroid nodules, partial or total thyroidectomy, mental health issues), gender, age, and 60 unique visual adornments (hats, beads, ties, glasses) (Fig. 3, Fig. 4). The game features a 2D point-and-click interface with buttons on the left and right sides of the home screen (Fig. 2), utilizing square colliders and a RayCast system for interaction. Basic personal care options include Sleeping (simulated by a "Zzz" particle system and sleep mask for 8 seconds, without health penalty) (Fig. 5.a), Exercise (three weight-lifting animations with speed adjusting to health) (Fig. 5.b), Care (heart particle system) (Fig. 5.c), and Feeding (eight healthy food options appearing randomly) (Fig. 6). Advanced medical care options, initially hidden and revealed when specific health conditions are met, include Mental Health support (speech bubbles simulating psychologist consultations), Thyroid Hormone Replacement/Antithyroid Medication, Radioactive Iodine Therapy (mimicked by a particle system) (Fig. 7.c), and Radiotherapy (triggered if radioactive iodine therapy is ineffective, featuring a stabilizing mask animation varying by nodule stage) (Fig. 7.c). The game incorporates a life system with a health bar (Fig. 2), calculated every 0.5 seconds using the formula `H = M - Dinitial + Σ Bi`, where `M` is the average of health maintenance contributions (care, nutrition, exercise, sleep, 0-85%), `Dinitial` is the sum of initial health deductions (Mental Health 10%, Hypothyroidism/Hyperthyroidism 15%, Tumor Level 1 20%, Tumor Level 2 30%, Tumor Level 3 40%, Tumor Level 4 50%), and `Σ Bi` is the sum of treatment health boosts (Mental Health 8%, Hypothyroidism/Hyperthyroidism 15%, Radioactive Iodine 20%, Radiotherapy 5%). A game timer runs clockwise in the HUD (Fig. 2), and animations are checked every 0.1 seconds, disabling interaction buttons during this time. The game includes a state machine that updates the thyroid character's condition every second based on player interactions (Fig. 8). Game over scenarios include natural death from old age (if life bar > 50% after a predefined period of iterations), health complications, or neglect (Fig. 9), with a tombstone displaying a happy or sad thyroid angel before restarting a new case.

- RESULTS AND METRICS:
The game underwent evaluation by three female thyroid health specialists, collectively possessing 12 to 23 years of experience. During individual sessions, they assessed six prerecorded game animations depicting common thyroid clinical cases (hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, thyroid cancer, nodules, radioactive iodine, radiotherapy). Specialists completed a qualitative User Experience form covering medical accuracy, effectiveness, usability, art and design quality, engagement, educational effectiveness, and empathy evocation. Key positive feedback included "Accurate disease coverage," "Engaging visuals," and "Valuable learning tool" (Fig. 10). Specialists praised the realistic portrayal of symptoms and effects on the thyroid gland, comprehensive and accurate clinical scenarios, intuitive game choice interactions, and original art and design (Fig. 1). They noted the game effectively communicates serious medical information in a captivating manner, strikes a balance between education and entertainment, and successfully captures attention while evoking empathy. One specialist, familiar with Tamagotchi-style games, particularly highlighted the "cute" visuals enhancing engagement.

- LIMITATIONS:
The current version of CancerST does not include surgical removal of the thyroid as a direct player-initiated treatment option, though post-surgical states are visually represented. Suggestions for future improvement include incorporating more diverse scenarios such as insomnia and cautioning against vigorous exercise during severe hyperthyroidism, emphasizing the importance of a low-iodine diet in interactive narratives, and tracking player progress over time. Furthermore, experts recommended underscoring the predominant use of surgical intervention for thyroid cancer, reserving radioactive iodine for more severe cases, and adding a final positive message highlighting the effectiveness of early detection and treatment.

- KEY CONCEPTS:
Serious Game, Virtual Pet, Tamagotchi-style, Thyroid Cancer, Hypothyroidism, Hyperthyroidism, Radioactive Iodine Therapy, Radiotherapy, Unity Engine, Gamified Learning, Health Management System, User Experience Evaluation, Iterative Development.
